definitions.gloss: shirabyoshi; female dancer-entertainer of the Heian and Kamakura periods
definitions.explanation: Female performers of the late Heian and Kamakura periods who danced and sang while dressed in male court attire (a white suikan robe and tall eboshi hat). The name comes from the simple, unaccompanied rhythm (白拍子) of their performances. Famous shirabyoshi include Shizuka Gozen and Giō.

examples.english: Shirabyoshi performed their dances dressed in men's clothing.

examples.japanese: {静御前|しずかごぜん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{白拍子|しらびょうし}だった。
examples.english: Shizuka Gozen was a famous shirabyoshi dancer.

examples.english: From the late Heian to the Kamakura period, shirabyoshi dancers were popular among nobles and warriors.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{白拍子|しらびょうし} originally referred to a style of song and dance performed to a simple beat without instrumental accompaniment. It later came to refer to the female performers themselves. Their distinctive feature was performing in ⟦{男装|だんそう}→男装：23925_dansou⟧ (male attire) — a {水干|すいかん} (white robe) and {烏帽子|えぼし} (tall court hat).

FAMOUS SHIRABYOSHI:
